description: Security & Compliance features: Access request workflow and Session recording
steps: Step 1 - Access Request Workflow: Create app/models/access_request.py with AccessRequest model (id int PK, requester_id FK users.id, resource_type enum: document/group, resource_id int, reason text, status enum: pending/approved/denied default pending, reviewed_by FK users.id nullable, reviewed_at DateTime nullable, created_at, updated_at). Create app/schemas/access_request.py with AccessRequestCreate (resource_type, resource_id, reason), AccessRequestResponse, AccessRequestReview (action: approve/deny). Create app/services/access_request.py with AccessRequestService that: (a) creates access request and sends notification to resource owner/admin via NotificationManager.create_notification, (b) approves request - updates status, sets reviewed_by/reviewed_at, grants permission (for groups: could add a GroupMembership or note; for documents: log the grant), (c) denies request - updates status with reviewer info. Create app/api/access_request.py with: POST /api/request-access (create request, any authenticated user), GET /api/access-requests (list pending requests, admin only), GET /api/access-requests/mine (list user's own requests), POST /api/access-requests/{id}/approve (admin), POST /api/access-requests/{id}/deny (admin). Register in router.py.

Step 2 - Session Recording: Create app/models/session.py with UserSession model (id str PK uuid, user_id FK users.id, started_at DateTime, ended_at DateTime nullable, ip_address str, user_agent str nullable) and SessionDocument model (id int PK, session_id FK user_sessions.id, document_id FK documents.id, action enum: view/download/edit, accessed_at DateTime). Create app/schemas/session.py with UserSessionResponse, SessionDocumentResponse, SessionListResponse. Create app/services/session_recording.py with SessionRecordingService that: (a) get_or_create_session - finds active session for user/IP or creates new one (sessions timeout after 30 min of inactivity), (b) record_document_access - adds SessionDocument entry (lightweight, non-blocking), (c) list_sessions - admin query with date range filter, (d) get_session_detail - returns session with all document accesses. Create app/middleware/session_recording.py as lightweight middleware that: only activates on document access routes (/api/documents/), extracts user from token (non-blocking, fails silently), records access. Alternative: use a FastAPI dependency/event hook approach instead of full middleware to keep it lightweight. Create app/api/sessions.py with: GET /api/sessions (admin, list sessions with date filters), GET /api/sessions/{id} (admin, session detail with documents accessed). Register in router.py. Integration: add a helper function that can be called from document view/download endpoints to record access.

Step 3 - Register all new models in app/models/__init__.py: Add imports for AccessRequest, UserSession, SessionDocument, ComplianceReport, GeoFenceRule, WatermarkConfig. Add to __all__ list. Ensure all new routers are registered in app/api/router.py.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/request-access creates an access request and sends notification
GET /api/access-requests returns pending requests for admins
POST /api/access-requests/{id}/approve updates status and grants access
UserSession model tracks sessions with IP and user agent
SessionDocument records individual document accesses within a session
GET /api/sessions returns session list for admins with date filtering
GET /api/sessions/{id} returns session detail with document access log
Session recording is lightweight and does not slow down requests
All models registered in __init__.py, all routers in router.py
verification: uv run python -m pytest tests/ -x -q (all tests pass)
